review: All ten sampled facts confirmed against cited sources; some stored excerpts cover only part of compound claims, so the reviewer checked their remaining clauses. This result is one qualification fixture, not an exhaustive model evaluation.

claims.concept: DATE criteria field types and formats
claims.claim: DATE criteria supports five date format types: ISODate (ISO-8601 formatted date, default), EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS (all Unix epoch timestamps requiring BSON type long), and OBJECT_ID.
claims.basis: Standard setup supports ISO date, three epoch units and ObjectId. Its following paragraph requires BSON long for the epoch formats. The independently re-fetched cited Terraform datasource confirms ISODATE as default.

claims.concept: DATE criteria field types and formats
claims.claim: The date field must be indexed for optimal archiving performance; Atlas issues an Index Sufficiency Warning if the ratio of documents scanned to documents returned is 10 or more.
claims.basis: Standard setup explicitly states the scanned-to-returned ratio threshold10 and requires indexing the date field.

claims.claim: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive DATE criteria supports exactly five date_format values: ISODATE, EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS, and OBJECT_ID.
claims.basis: The five formats occur in the cited standard setup; the cited Terraform datasource names all five values.

claims.claim: The date field used for archival criteria cannot be modified after the online archive is created.
claims.basis: The cited standard setup forbids modifying the date field after creation. The stored time-field excerpt also agrees for time series.

claims.claim: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive calculates document age using the formula: current_date > dateField + expireAfterDays. When this condition is true, documents are nominated for archival.
claims.basis: The cited API criteria.dateField description gives the exact date-plus-days inequality and archival purpose.

claims.concept: Partition fields constraints for DATE rules
claims.claim: Partition field values are limited to a maximum of 700 characters; documents with partition field values exceeding this limit are not archived.
claims.basis: The cited Terraform resource partition_fields paragraph states the700-character limit and excludes longer documents.

claims.concept: Partition fields constraints for DATE rules
claims.claim: For DATE criteria (Date Match), the date field used for archiving must be included as one of the partition fields and is positioned first by default in the partition path.
claims.basis: The cited standard setup places the date field first by default. Its note and the cited Terraform criteria note require the date field among partition keys.

claims.claim: Time series collections in Atlas Online Archive must use DATE criteria type; CUSTOM criteria is not supported for time series collection types.
claims.basis: The cited Terraform resource criteria section requires DATE for TIMESERIES; the cited overview describes its time-field-plus-days rule.

claims.claim: DATE criteria selects a single date field and an age in days; only the age parameter can be modified after archive creation, not the chosen date field.
claims.basis: The cited standard setup defines Date Match and fixes the date field. The independently re-fetched cited yossale article explicitly limits Date Match edits to the number of days. Primary manage-online-archive docs also confirm age-limit edits.

claims.claim: Custom Criteria accepts standard MongoDB query filter expressions to define archival conditions.
claims.basis: The cited overview defines a custom query selecting archive documents. Its standard setup link explains the normal MongoDB find filter. The claim is about filter expressions and does not imply support for every query operator.
